texts.facts: Brief facts of the case are as under:- 2.1 On 26-4-2012 between 11:30 and 12:00 pm. deceased was working in the agriculture farm of Vallabhbhai Vastabhai Patoliya and for the purpose of laying down manure in the said NEUTRAL CITATION C/SA/13/2020 ORDER DATED: Paschim Gujarat Vij Company Limited ... vs L/H Of Deceaed Jignesh Jamanbhai Gohil on 4 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171781391/ 1 04/07/2024 undefined farm the deceased had climbed on the top of the tractor's trolley which was in vertical condition through hydraulic jack and there by the deceased was pushing the manure by his legs towards the land which was loaded in the tractor trolley at that point of time deceased came into the contact with the loose and hanging electricity line passing through the said farm and got electricuted and died on the spot. 2.2 Legal heirs and representatives of respondent No.1 filed suit before the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Junagadh being Regular Civil Suit no 279/2014 claiming compensation of Rs.3 lakh. The suit was dismissed. 2.3 Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, the legal heirs and representatives of respondent No.1 filed regular appeal before the Ld. Principal District judge Junagadh being Regular Civil Appeal no. 33/2017. 3. Hence, present second appeal. Though served, none appears for the respondents.
texts.arguments: Learned advocate for the appellant for admission of the appeal would submit that the learned appellate Court has erroneously referred and relied upon Rule 77 of the Indian Electricity Rules, 1956 (in short "the Rules") to believe that the electricity line should be hanged more than 6.1 mtr height from the ground. He would further submit that Rule 77 of the Rules is mainly applicable for the streets in the city and not in the agricultural field. He would further submit that considering the panchnama of the place at Exh.26 and considering the overall aspect, the appellant was not negligent in causing death of minor, but the minor himself, as he without remained vigilant, came in contact with 11 kv electricity line and got electrocuted, but the learned appellate Court has committed serious error in granting decree in favour of the plaintiff . 5.1 Learned advocate Mr. Dave submits to admit this appeal on the following no substantial questions of law:- "(A) Whether the Hon'ble First Appellate Court has erred in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the Hon'ble Trial Court? Learned advocate for the appellant submits that the learned appellate Court has committed serious error in interpreting Rule 77 of the Rules. On the other hand if the question was practically covered by the decision of the highest court or if the general principles to be applied in determining the question are well settled and the only question was of applying those principles to the particular facts of the case it would not be a substantial question of law. 28.
